source_evidence: A fund’s past performance is not as important as you might think because past performance does not predict future returns. But past performance can tell you how volatile or stable a fund has been over a period of time. The more volatile the fund, the higher the investment risk.
answer: When evaluating an ETF, don’t treat its past returns as a forecast of what it will earn in the future. Its past performance can still help you understand how much its value has fluctuated over a period of time. Greater volatility indicates higher investment risk, so past performance offers context about risk—not a guarantee of future results.
